events.title: Solar eclipse halts a battle between Lydia and Media
events.description: According to Herodotus, day turned to night during a battle on the Halys river, and the armies made peace. Astronomers date the eclipse to 28 May 585 BCE, one of the earliest precisely dated events.
events.html: According to Herodotus, day turned to night during a battle on the Halys river, and the armies made peace. Astronomers date the eclipse to 28 May 585 BCE, one of the earliest precisely dated events.

events.title: Li Shimin captures Dou Jiande at the Battle of Hulao
events.description: The Tang prince Li Shimin, besieging Wang Shichong in Luoyang, held the Hulao Pass against Dou Jiande's relieving Xia army, routed it and captured Dou. Wang surrendered soon after, and the victory gave the Tang control of the North China Plain.

events.title: King Æthelstan begins his invasion of Scotland
events.description: The English king Æthelstan, first king of all England since 927, invaded Scotland by land and sea with a large force. No record of any battles fought during the invasion has survived, and Æthelstan returned to England later in the year.

events.title: Andrew Jackson signs the Indian Removal Act
events.description: The law authorised the president to exchange lands west of the Mississippi for Native territory in the East. It led to the forced removals known as the Trail of Tears, in which thousands died.
events.html: The law authorised the president to exchange lands west of the Mississippi for Native territory in the East. It led to the forced removals known as the Trail of Tears, in which thousands died.

events.title: Paris Commune falls after the 'Bloody Week'
events.description: The last Communard defenders were overcome around the Père Lachaise cemetery. Government troops killed thousands during the week, and the Commune became a lasting symbol for the left.
events.html: The last Communard defenders were overcome around the Père Lachaise cemetery. Government troops killed thousands during the week, and the Commune became a lasting symbol for the left.

events.title: Azerbaijan and Armenia declare independence
events.description: As the short-lived Transcaucasian federation broke up, the Azerbaijan Democratic Republic and the Republic of Armenia proclaimed independence. Both were absorbed by Soviet Russia in 1920.
events.html: As the short-lived Transcaucasian federation broke up, the Azerbaijan Democratic Republic and the Republic of Armenia proclaimed independence. Both were absorbed by Soviet Russia in 1920.

events.title: King Leopold III surrenders the Belgian army
events.description: After eighteen days of fighting, Leopold III capitulated to Germany against his government's wishes. The surrender exposed the Allied flank as the Dunkirk evacuation gathered pace.

events.title: Pakistan carries out nuclear tests in Balochistan
events.description: Pakistan detonated nuclear devices in the Chagai Hills, responding to India's tests earlier that month. Both countries now stood as declared nuclear powers.
